g.text: Where NVIDIA's moat is deep, contested or thin (repo verdicts, Nov 2026)

text.tspan: Green = deep moat (4-5) · Amber = contested (3-3.5) · Red = thin (1-2)
↗ gap widening → stable ↘ narrowing · $ = where NVIDIA books gross profit directly

g.text: SOFTWARE & SERVICES — defends the margin, earns little directly
SILICON & SUPPLY — the profit engine and its gatekeeper

text.tspan: 13 · Ecosystem, GTM & capital — 4.0 ↘
~$99B of stakes; Broadcom AI revenue ~12% → ~19% of NVIDIA DC
12 · Orchestration & cloud — 2.0 →
hyperscalers own the customer, control plane and their own chips
11 · Inference software — 3.0 →
open engines (vLLM, SGLang) run on rivals; rack-scale serving still leads
10 · Libraries (CUDA-X) — 4.5 → deepest moat
no rival leads in any of 15 library domains
lock-in 4.5/5 for enterprises, 2.75/5 for frontier labs
08 · Systems, racks & AI factories — 4.0 ↘ $
~$35B of a $50-60B gigawatt; AMD Helios ships from end Q3 2026
07 · DPU, SuperNIC & storage — 3.0 ↘
captive offload (Nitro, Titanium); storage software goes to partners
06 · Scale-out networking — 3.0 → $
~$17.5B a quarter (Est.); Broadcom leads switch silicon
05 · Scale-up (NVLink) — 4.0 ↘ $
72-GPU domain in volume; Helios and UALink (2027) close in
04 · CPU (Grace, Vera) — 2.0 →
~2% of a Vera Rubin rack; rivals out-core Vera
03 · Memory, packaging & supply — 4.0 ↗ only widening gap
$279B of commitments; ~60% of 2026 CoWoS (Est.)
02 · GPU silicon — 3.0 ↘ $$$
profit engine; AMD MI455X matches Rubin on paper
